chunks: Abu Ja'far Muhammad b. 'Ali b. al-Husayn b. Musa b. Babawayh al-Qummi (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Musa b. al-Mutawakkil (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: 'Abdullah b. Ja'far al-Himyari narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. al-Husayn b. Abi'l Khattab narrated to us from al-Hasan b. Mahbub from Abi Ayyub from Muhammad b. Muslim from Abi Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him). He said: I heard him say:
How beautiful are good deeds after sins! And how ugly are sins after good deeds!

key_terms.السَّيِّئَات: sins / evil deeds — wrongful actions that distance one from Allah
key_terms.الْحَسَنَات: good deeds — virtuous actions that draw one closer to Allah

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Baqir say about good deeds after sins and sins after good deeds?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) expresses a profound moral insight through rhetorical exclamation: the beauty of repentance and turning back to good deeds after committing sins, and the ugliness of falling into sin after performing good deeds. This teaching was transmitted through an established chain including Muhammad b. Muslim, one of the prominent companions of the Imam, and emphasizes the dynamic nature of one's spiritual state — that neither virtue nor sin is a permanent destination, but rather one's current trajectory is what defines one's spiritual beauty or ugliness.
